findings.what: The lesson never says why anyone compounds a train when one 12 : 108 pair would also give 9 : 1, though the brief promised it and the research holds it (one pair stops at about 10 : 1, and marine reduction boxes add a second train past 10 : 1), so add to screen 10: "One pair stops at about 10 : 1. Past that, the wheel grows huge beside its pinion. So a bigger ratio takes a second stage."

findings.where: Screen 3 (Count the turns), the revolution counters
findings.what: Before Check, both middle-shaft counters read "6 turns", which does the first stage for him and shows the value of the 6-turn slip, so show "? turns" on the middle shaft too until he checks.
In "They make one turn of the output wheel" it is unclear what "they" means, so write "Those three turns make one turn of the output wheel."
Screen 3's hint and slips and screen 4's text use "stage" before any screen says what one is, so add "Each meshed pair is one stage." to screen 2 or to the start of screen 4.

findings.where: Screen 8 picture (winch train) and screen 11 picture (equal stages)
findings.what: The 12- and 10-tooth pinions on screen 8 and the 15-tooth pinions on screen 11 are drawn smaller than their 32 × 22 tooth-count tags, so the tags hide the gears and their meshes. On screen 8 the "60" and "10" tags also sit 2 units apart on one line and read as "60 10". Use smaller tags on small gears, or move the wheel's count onto its face away from the pinion.

findings.where: Screen 1 heading and the "The 36-tooth wheel" button at 360 px
findings.what: Both break across lines at the hyphen ("12-" / "tooth pinion", "The 36-" / "tooth wheel"), so use a non-breaking hyphen in the "n-tooth" names on screens 1 and 12.

findings.where: Screen 13 (Three stages), after a right answer
findings.what: Once solved, the motor can be turned by hand and the output's marked tooth shows which way it goes, which answers screen 14 in advance, so leave the motor unturnable on screen 13 as the build log meant.
"In an ideal train the power, torque × speed, stays the same" puts an aside mid-sentence, so write "Power is torque × speed. In an ideal train it stays the same."
"It does, even though it has the same 12 teeth as the motor's pinion" reads awkwardly, so write "It has the same 12 teeth as the motor's pinion, yet it turns three times slower."
